The story primarily unfolds in "real-time," matching the story time closely to the reading time as Ilse and Jonas have a brief, tense interaction at the ferry dock and inside the hut. Rather than compressing large spans of time or dramatically stretching a single instant, the author uses measured, deliberate pacing. Small actions—such as coiling a rope, hanging up a coat, or picking up a dropped invoice—are placed between clipped lines of dialogue. This slightly slows down the rhythm of the scene, effectively creating a sense of awkwardness, unspoken history, and quiet tension between the two characters. Brief references to the past ("Früher hatte er immer...", "Seit immer") compress years of shared history into passing thoughts without disrupting the grounded, immediate flow of the present moment.
